battle.name: 唐奪長安之戰
battle.brief: 乾符四年十一月，沙陀節度使李克用引河東精騎自河中南下，圍逼長安；大齊守將尚讓出城迎戰，唐騎乘勢破之，黃巢焚城夜走，李克用入城。攻城時唐軍備有發石車、雲梯、撞車等器械，投石機用於壓制城頭與摧毀木柵，惟此役制勝關鍵在騎兵奇襲與守軍自潰。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 交戰一方是唐僖宗朝廷。僖宗自廣明元年冬出奔成都之後，關中宿衛與中央禁軍盡失，中央軍政全賴各道藩鎮供兵，京師收復後的守備仍由河中、西川與京西北諸鎮軍分屯關隘與城坊。另一方是大齊政權：黃巢自稱齊帝，以尚讓、葛從周等部將分領兵權，兵眾多為關中、河南一帶流動作戰的起義眾與歸附散兵，糧秣全靠劫掠與臨時徵發維持，軍令難以統一。真正推動收復長安的，是河東節度使李克用率領的沙陀騎兵，先鋒為彍騎等精騎，號令嚴整，騎射見長，由河中蒲州出發沿渭水南下；河中節度使王重榮既已反正，蒲州又是關中儲糧與轉運的樞紐，使唐軍得以不斷補充箭矢、糧秣與攻城器械。換言之，這不是中央對地方的戰爭，而是朝廷靠一支外來騎軍收復自己的國都，而收復的功勞與後果也一併落到這支騎軍與其首領身上。
countriesEn: One side was the court of Emperor Xizong of Tang, but a court stripped of its own military: after the emperor fled to Chengdu in the winter of 880, the palace guards of Guanzhong and the central imperial army were gone, and government rested on troops supplied by the regional circuits, with garrisons from Hezhong, Xichuan and the northwestern jiedushi still holding the passes and city wards once the capital was recovered. The other side was the state of Great Qi proclaimed by Huang Chao, who styled himself Emperor of Qi and divided command among generals such as Shang Rang and Ge Congzhou; his ranks were filled largely with insurgent bands on the move through Guanzhong and Henan together with surrendered soldiers, sustained by foraging and ad hoc requisition, and his orders were never uniform. The force that actually retook Chang'an was the Shatuo cavalry of Li Keyong, jiedushi of Hedong, whose vanguard was the elite Wo cavalry: strict in discipline, pre-eminent in riding and shooting, and moving south from Puzhou in Hezhong along the Wei River. Wang Chongrong, jiedushi of Hezhong, had already thrown off Huang Chao, and Puzhou was the hub of grain storage and transport for Guanzhong, so the Tang army could be fed and resupplied with arrows, provisions and siege gear. In other words this was not central authority against local authority; it was a court buying back its own capital with a foreign host, and both the credit and the consequences of that recovery went to that host and to its commander.
people: 李克用（856－908）是本役的決定人物。沙陀人，父世為沙陀騎帥，他幼年隨父內附唐朝，以驍勇善騎射顯名，至此已任河東節度使、檢校太尉，號雁門郡王，人稱李鴉兒。他以騎兵追討黃巢數年，屢破齊軍，883年冬率師自河中直趨長安，是全役的指揮核心，其沙陀軍的騎射與奔襲速度決定了戰局。黃巢（820－884）為起義領袖，880年十二月引眾突破潼關直入長安，建大齊稱帝，至883年焚城北走，翌年六月在泰山狼虎谷為部下尚讓所殺。大齊大將尚讓早於877年便被授予兵部尚書，883年冬奉命守長安，出城迎戰一戰而敗，隨後與黃巢同夜出逃，後追至狼虎谷，親手弒其主。河中節度使王重榮原為黃巢所破，被迫反正，據蒲州以拒齊軍，恰恰為唐軍打開了進兵與運糧的通道，功勞不亞於前線血戰。僖宗李儇在成都聞捷，二年之後自蜀道還京師，重建朝廷樞紐。另有河東、朔方各鎮與京西北諸處守軍配合封鎖道路，形成對長安的合圍之勢。
peopleEn: Li Keyong (856-908) is the decisive figure of this campaign. A Shatuo, born into a line of Shatuo cavalry commanders, he entered Tang service as a boy when his father's clan submitted, and made his name through boldness and his skill with the bow and the saddle; by now he was jiedushi of Hedong, holder of the title Inspector-in-Chief, known by the style of Prince of Yanmen, and popularly called Li the Crow. He had chased Huang Chao for years with cavalry, breaking Qi armies repeatedly, and in the winter of 883 he led his host straight from Hezhong toward Chang'an; the whole battle turned on the shooting and the running pace of his Shatuo riders. Huang Chao (820-884), the leader of the rebellion, had broken through the Tong Pass in December 880, marched into Chang'an, founded Great Qi and proclaimed himself emperor; in 883 he burned the city and fled north, and in June of the following year he was killed by his own general Shang Rang in Wolf Tiger Valley on Mount Tai. Shang Rang had been appointed Minister of War as early as 877, and when he was left to hold Chang'an in the winter of 883 he came out to meet the Tang army, was beaten in a single engagement, and fled the city that same night with Huang Chao, later catching up the fugitive in Wolf Tiger Valley and killing him with his own hand. Wang Chongrong, jiedushi of Hezhong, had earlier been broken by Huang Chao and turned against him, holding Puzhou against the Qi forces; in doing so he opened the very road by which troops and grain would reach the Tang army, and his contribution was scarcely less than that of the men who fought in the front line. Emperor Xizong heard the news at Chengdu and, two years later, returned over the road from Shu to the imperial capital, rebuilding the machinery of government. Other garrisons from Hedong, Shuofang and the northwest supported the operation by sealing the roads, so that Chang'an was ringed from several directions at once.
kits: 本卡兵器是投石機（onager），即以扭力絞盤蓄能、以槓桿甩出的拋石器，唐人稱發石車、拋石車或霹靂車。其源流可溯至希臘與羅馬的同型機：公元前250年前後羅馬已用扭力式投石機攻城，設計早於唐一千餘年，東傳與自製的傳統並行；漢末三國已有實例，《三國志》裴注引袁宏《英雄記》記諸葛亮造發石車以供軍用，曹魏攻鄴城時審配亦用霹靂車破城垣，隋唐攻守器械中投石車沿用不衰。它在唐軍攻城體系中屬重器械一類，負責壓制城頭守軍、摧毀城柵與在缺口處打開通路，與雲梯、撞車、鈎拒、飛火（火箭）配套：撞車撞門，雲梯與巢車登城，飛火燒毀木柭，投石車則列於後方陣地發射，射程數百步，石彈重達數十斤，可在遠距離打擊城頭人物與木構防禦。守城的大齊軍以木柵、拒馬、弩機與隨時修整的城防抵擋，並以騎兵出城反擊。惟本役文獻未詳舉投石機實際發射的次數與所毀目標，其作用應在封鎖城東通道、掩護接近與震懾城頭，而非攻城的主手段。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the onager, a torsion-powered stone-thrower wound by a winch and released by a throwing arm, known in Tang sources as the fa-shi-che, the pao-shi-che or the thunder carriage. Its lineage runs back to the Hellenistic and Roman machines of the same name: Roman torsion onagers were already throwing stones at city walls around 250 BC, over a thousand years before the Tang, and imported designs ran alongside locally built ones. China had working examples by the late Han and the Three Kingdoms: the Pei Songzhi commentary to the Records of the Three Kingdoms, quoting Yuan Hong's Record of Heroes, notes that Zhuge Liang built stone-throwing engines to supply his army, and when Cao Wei besieged Ye, Shen Pei used a thunder carriage to break the wall; the throwing engine was never dropped from Tang siege and defence inventories. Within the Tang assault system it counted as heavy equipment, responsible for pinning the defenders on the wall, smashing the palisade and opening a breach, and it worked in concert with scaling ladders, battering rams, hook-poles and fire-arrows: rams to strike the gates, ladders and siege-towers to scale, fire-arrows to burn the wooden defences, while the onager stood in the rear of the formation and fired at a range of several hundred paces, its stone missiles weighing several tens of jin and able to strike the heads of defenders and wooden structures from a distance. On the Qi side, the garrison answered with timber palisades, cheval-de-frise, crossbow platforms and a city wall kept in constant repair, and sent cavalry out of the gates to counterattack. The documents of this particular campaign do not set out how often the throwing engines were actually fired or what they destroyed; their part was to seal the eastern approach, cover the advance and terrify the wall, not to carry the assault.
tactics: 唐軍取長安走的是西北方向的捷徑：李克用先掃清河東、克復河中蒲州，取得關東的出發點與糧源，再沿渭水與黃河之間的通道南下，兵鋒直指長安城東。883年十一月大軍抵渭，黃巢派尚讓率精兵出城，列陣於城東迎戰；李克用不與之久纏，以沙陀騎兵的高速機動繞擊側翼，一戰即摧垮其陣，兵鋒直抵城牆之下。城內人心隨之崩潰，黃巢當夜焚燒宮室、府庫與木構建築，與尚讓等率殘部由城門北出，取道藍田，轉入商山山地；唐騎一路追擊，齊軍在藍田一帶潰散，士卒多散。沙陀騎兵追出長安之後並未急著掃清關中殘敵，而是緊咬黃巢主力不放，追過洛陽，迫使黃巢焚城而走，再北渡黃河入河北，一路奔竄至泰山狼虎谷。收城之後的另一層教訓是紀律：沙陀軍入城即縱掠市坊，禁軍與朝廷禁卒無力制止，直至僖宗還都、遣使曉諭才略為收斂，可見以私募精銳取國都必然要付出秩序上的代價。
tacticsEn: The Tang army took the short road in from the north-west: Li Keyong first cleared Hedong and recovered Hezhong and Puzhou, gaining a launchpad in the east of the passes and a source of grain, and then moved down the corridor between the Wei River and the Yellow River with his point aimed at the east side of Chang'an. In the eleventh month of 883 the host reached the Wei; Huang Chao sent Shang Rang out of the city with picked troops and arrayed them to meet the attack east of the walls. Li Keyong did not stand and trade blows with them; he used the speed of his Shatuo cavalry to swing around the flank, and the Qi line came apart in a single action, the assault riding right up to the foot of the wall. Morale inside collapsed with it. That night Huang Chao fired the palaces, the storehouses and the wooden structures, and with Shang Rang and a few others left the city by the northern gate for Lantian and the hills of the Shang range; the Tang cavalry pursued and the Qi troops disintegrated around Lantian, most of them scattering. After riding out of Chang'an the Shatuo did not pause to mop up the scattered Qi bands in Guanzhong but kept hard on the heels of Huang Chao's main body, pursued him through Luoyang, forced him to burn that city and run, followed him north across the Yellow River into Hebei and chased him all the way to Wolf Tiger Valley on Mount Tai. A second lesson of the campaign was one of discipline: as soon as the Shatuo entered the city they began stripping the wards and markets, and neither the imperial guards nor the palace troops had the strength to stop them; only when Xizong was back in the capital and sent out envoys with admonitions did the plundering ease. Recovering a capital with a private host of this kind, in other words, exacts a price in public order.
data: 時間線短而密：乾符四年（883）十一月李克用自河中出師逼長安，十二月城破，黃巢出走，自前鋒抵渭到城陷不過一月；其後黃巢北奔至狼虎谷被殺，中和四年（884）六月首級傳至京師，歷時約半年。距離上，潼關至長安官道約二百餘里，黃巢棄長安北出潼關、轉入洛陽，全程數百里；洛陽以北至泰山狼虎谷又是數百里的追擊路，兼有平原與山地。兵員上，黃巢起義初期聚眾數十萬，史書往往記作六十萬，攻入長安時的隊伍仍以萬計；唐廷一方則只剩各道藩鎮臨時徵集的兵力，與李克用麾下數萬沙陀騎兵，其中彍騎為精銳，歐陽修《五代史》形容其百步馳射、攢射一發人馬皆辟易，反映的是射擊集群而非全軍的戰力。器械數量無從核實，只能從用法推知：投石車一次齊射可覆蓋數百步的城頭，石彈重數十斤，發射需十數人合力拉絞；雲梯、撞車、飛火按攻城梯次配置，損耗與補充都依賴河中與軍中所備的木材、繩索、桐油與火藥，而河中到渭水的運糧線長度是這支部隊在關中能撐多久的實際指標。
dataEn: The timeline is short and dense. In the eleventh month of 883 Li Keyong marched out of Hezhong to press Chang'an; the city fell in the twelfth month, Huang Chao fled, and less than a month separated the arrival of the vanguard at the Wei from the breach. Huang Chao was killed at Wolf Tiger Valley and his head reached the capital in the sixth month of 884, so the whole affair ran about half a year from end to end. As for distances, the official road from Tong Pass to Chang'an is a little over two hundred li, and Huang Chao's flight north through Tong Pass and on toward Luoyang covered several hundred li; from Luoyang north to Wolf Tiger Valley lay several hundred li more of pursuit road across plain and hill country. On numbers of men, Huang Chao had gathered tens of thousands in the early days of the rising, with the histories often putting the figure at six hundred thousand, and the host that entered Chang'an was still numbered in myriads; on the Tang side nothing remained but troops hastily raised by the circuits together with the several tens of thousands of Shatuo riders under Li Keyong, the elite among them being the Wo cavalry, whom Ouyang Xiu in his History of the Five Dynasties described as shooting at a hundred paces and bringing down men and horses in a single volley - a picture of concentrated archery, not of the whole army. The number of machines cannot be verified and can only be inferred from how they were used: one salvo of the throwing engines could sweep several hundred paces of wall, the stones weighed several tens of jin, and firing required a dozen men or more working the winch; scaling ladders, battering rams and fire-arrows were allotted by assault echelon, and their losses and replacements depended on the timber, rope, tung oil and propellant stored at Hezhong and in the camp. The length of the grain line from Hezhong to the Wei was in practice the measure of how long this army could hold together in Guanzhong.
cause: 這場戰爭的直接起因，是唐廷在丟失京師三年之後借外軍收復首都。廣明元年（880）十二月黃巢大軍突破潼關、徑入長安，僖宗僅帶少數人出奔成都，關中州縣望風崩潰，兩京陷落令唐的行政中斷了近三年。深層原因則是起義軍在流竄中吸收大量潰兵與流民，人數膨脹而戰鬥力未同步提高，糧秣與補給線拉得過長，關中已難支撐其長期屯駐，軍紀亦隨之鬆散。朝廷方面則自河東、朔方招沙陀兵討賊，李克用受命於河東，逐步收復汾、代、忻、蔚諸州，把黃巢在北方的游騎逐出，形成從西北壓下來的攻勢；河中方面，王重榮本為黃巢所破，懼而反正，河中一線落入唐軍手中。於是唐廷不待中央軍力恢復，便以李克用部為先鋒、王重榮為後援，合兵指向長安，而大齊政權在城下的崩解也由此注定。
causeEn: The immediate occasion of this war was a court that, having lost its capital for three years, borrowed foreign troops to take it back. In December 880 Huang Chao's host broke through Tong Pass and marched into Chang'an; the emperor fled to Chengdu with only a handful of men, the prefectures of Guanzhong collapsed at the news, and the fall of the two capitals left Tang administration interrupted for close to three years. The deeper cause lay in the rebel army itself: by absorbing deserters and refugees as it moved, the rising swelled in numbers without a corresponding growth in fighting power, its supply line grew too long, Guanzhong could no longer sustain its stationary presence there, and discipline loosened accordingly. On the court side, the Tang had enlisted Shatuo troops from Hedong and Shuofang to fight the rebellion, and Li Keyong, appointed in Hedong, recovered Fenzhou, Daizhou, Xinzhou and Weizhou one after another, driving Huang Chao's northern raiding bands away and creating an offensive that pressed down from the north-west. In Hezhong, Wang Chongrong, who had earlier been broken by Huang Chao, turned in fear against him, and that line fell back into Tang hands. The court therefore did not wait for its own strength to recover: it set Li Keyong's army in the van and Wang Chongrong's behind it, and moved on Chang'an. The collapse of the Qi regime beneath the city walls was settled by the same combination.
impact: 長安復得之後，唐室的國運並未轉危為安，反而看得更清楚：收復京畿靠的是藩鎮與外來騎軍，中央直轄的禁軍與宿衛已無力單獨承擔守土之責，於是收復的過程本身就是藩鎮權力的一次擴張，李克用因功進封晉王，河東自此成為晚唐最具軍力的藩鎮之一，唐廷對河東既倚重又防備，終成心腹大患。更深一層的後果是，黃巢之死使中原戰線崩解，齊軍殘部或降或散，朝廷得以騰出兵力次第平定江淮與河東，但收拾殘局、鎮壓方鎮、重建漕運的漫長消耗，把唐帝國推向崩潰的邊緣：黃巢之亂後僅二十餘年，朱溫即行篡唐，帝號的延續靠的不再是制度而是刀兵。物質與制度層面，長安宮室、府庫與寺觀在焚城中大批毀壞，兩京所藏圖籍、鐘鼎與禮器散佚於兵火與遷徙，唐代考古與文獻研究此後不得不倚靠其他出土材料補闕；而朝廷為籌措軍費反覆加徵與括取財貨，又加深了藩鎮與中央的裂痕。
impactEn: Recovering Chang'an did not set the Tang house on firmer ground; it made the danger plainer. The capital had been retaken by a circuit army and a foreign host, and the central guards and palace troops were no longer capable of holding a city on their own. Recovery was therefore itself an enlargement of the power of the provincial governors: Li Keyong was advanced in rank for his service, Hedong became one of the strongest military bases of the late Tang, and the court could neither do without Hedong nor feel safe before it - a grievance at the heart of the dynasty's last years. At a deeper level, the death of Huang Chao broke up the rebel front in the north, so that the court could release troops to settle the Yangtze and Huai regions and Hedong in turn; but the long process of mopping up, disciplining the governors and rebuilding the grain transport drained the empire toward collapse. Barely more than twenty years after the rising, Zhu Wen usurped the dynasty: from then on the imperial title rested on the sword rather than on institutions. On the material and institutional side, the burning of the city destroyed palaces, storehouses and temples on a great scale, and the maps, books, bronze vessels and ritual objects of the two capitals were scattered by war and by migration, so that Tang archaeology and textual study have had to lean on other excavated material to fill the gaps; meanwhile the court's repeated levies and seizures of wealth to pay for the war widened the rift between the centre and the circuits.
result: 883年十二月，李克用大軍自城東入長安，大齊政權在關中的統治中樞就此崩解。黃巢焚燒宮室與積聚，與尚讓等率殘部北走，途中在藍田被沙陀騎兵追擊，部眾潰散，李克用追過洛陽，迫使黃巢焚城而走。追擊最終在泰山狼虎谷收束：884年六月，黃巢為部下所殺，首級傳京師，僖宗下詔大赦，齊軍舊部相繼歸降，唐廷由此重新控制兩京。對唐室而言，結果是一半的成功一半的代價：國都回來了，首領死了，但收復的功勞歸了河東，禁軍的重建與京畿的恢復仍需數年，地方割據的格局反而更牢。此後十餘年的中原秩序，靠的是刀兵而非制度維持，這一局面最終在朱溫代唐時走到盡頭。就本戰役本身而言，883年冬的長安之役是一場以騎兵機動與守軍自潰為轉折的奪城戰，而不是一場以攻城器械見長的殲滅戰；投石機一類重器械在唐軍編制中依然重要，但真正把城門打開的，是沙陀騎兵的速度與大齊內部的崩解。
resultEn: In December 883 Li Keyong's host entered Chang'an from the east and the seat of Qi rule in Guanzhong came apart. Huang Chao fired the palaces and the accumulated stores, and with Shang Rang and a few others headed north; on the way the Qi troops were caught by the Shatuo cavalry around Lantian and broke up, while Li Keyong pursued through Luoyang and forced Huang Chao to burn that city as well. The pursuit ended in Wolf Tiger Valley on Mount Tai: in June 884 Huang Chao was killed by his own men, his head was carried to the capital, Xizong issued a general amnesty, and the surviving Qi troops surrendered in bands, so that the court regained control of both capitals. For the Tang the result was half success and half cost: the capital was back and the rebel leader was dead, but the credit for the recovery belonged to Hedong, the rebuilding of the imperial guards and the restoration of the capital districts still took years, and the pattern of regional separatism grew more entrenched. The order of the central plain in the decade that followed was kept by armed force rather than by institutions, and that state of affairs finally ran its course when Zhu Wen replaced the Tang. As for the campaign itself, the winter of 883 was a seizure of a city decided by cavalry movement and by the collapse of the garrison from within, not a battle of annihilation fought with siege machines; engines like the onager still held their place in the Tang order of battle, but what actually opened the gates was the speed of the Shatuo horse and the disintegration of the Qi regime within the walls.
